utterances.text: And knowing that the tenant has this right could also make owners less willing to take a chance on these new and growing businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joanne
utterances.text: And I think that's the biggest issue from the young and growing businesses, that they won't get opportunities for leases as quickly.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joanne
utterances.text: Because they will have the problem of, I don't know if these guys are going to make it, but I'm going to have to deal with them anyway for another year.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joanne
utterances.text: Anyway, thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joanne
utterances.text: I have more to say, but I only got two minutes like everybody else.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joanne
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amauris Gurujung
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Zach Steinberg of the Real Estate Board of New York supports Intro 90's transparency provisions but opposes the mandatory lease extension, arguing it disrupts transactions and disadvantages new businesses. REBNY supports Intro 874's voluntary incentive model as a better approach.
chapters.title: Zach Steinberg of REBNY testifies on Intro 90 and Intro 874

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Thomas Henry and Councilman Burr-Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: My name is Zach Steinberg, and I'm testifying on behalf of the Real Estate Board of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to comment on the legislation before the committee today, and I'll focus my remarks on Intro 90 and Intro 874.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: New York's storefront market is healthy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Small businesses are driving the recovery.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Mom-and-pop businesses are opening and expanding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Availability is tightening in many corridors, and rents remain below previous highs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: This progress reflects the reality that owners and tenants are not adversaries.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: They are partners and work together to ensure that successful storefronts continue to thrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Rebney supports aspects of Intro 90, as the bill would help small...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: businesses enter lease negotiations with greater information and certainty.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Provisions we support include clear written leases, reasonable advance notice, accessible model documents, access to legal advice, and clear disclosures of property history.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: However, we have serious concerns with the provision that allows tenants to unilaterally extend their lease for up to one year when the parties cannot agree on a renewal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Beyond property right concerns, this could disrupt transactions already underway and delay a new business that has signed a lease, invested in the space, hired employees, and planned around a firm opening date.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: It could also make owners more cautious to leasing to newer businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: If owners can't rely on the agreed expiration date, they will have more reason to prioritize established, well-capitalized tenants over new restaurants, retailers, and first-time entrepreneurs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: This would undermine the small businesses we are all trying to support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: We believe Intro 874 is a better model.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: REBNY supports targeted city incentives that help legacy businesses remain in their communities when owners and tenants voluntarily reach long-term agreements.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: That approach incentivizes collaboration without mandating a particular lease outcome.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: We urge the Council to preserve Intro 90's transparency notice provisions, remove the mandatory extension, and advance practical voluntary tools like Intro 874 that help small businesses succeed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Zach Steinberg
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amauris Gurujung
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Brewer pushes back on the brokers' characterization of a healthy retail market, citing her experience that mom-and-pop businesses struggle to reach landlords and face dramatic rent increases. She notes that the 'next entrepreneur' is often a chain store and emphasizes the need for teeth to protect small businesses.
chapters.title: Council Member Brewer responds to broker panel on rent negotiation realities for mom-and-pop stores

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amauris Gurujung
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I thank everybody for your testimony, and I know that the portion that you bring up is controversial.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Don't forget commercial rent control is still something that people are talking about, and I am not in this bill.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So just be aware of that because it's hovering.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So the concept is...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: to try to come up with, I do disagree with the notion that it's not hard to talk to the owner, the owner's willing to get back to you.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's not my experience.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: In Manhattan, it's challenging, but even in our tour recently in Jackson Heights, I mean, there were just numerous examples with a bid.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Or at least the Chamber of Commerce working with them, that it was really hard to get the owner and the mom and pop to talk.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And the rents were going up dramatically.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I know you're thinking it's sort of a good retail situation, but for the mom and pop, it's really hard.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Now, if you own your building, if you have a condo, if you have a good relationship in a Michelama, for instance, where the...

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Residents are quite willing to work with the commercial.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: That's one thing.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But it's rough for these smaller businesses.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I guess what I'm saying is I think some teeth to the person who is in that business is needed, and there may be some other suggestions.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I do know that this notion that we are waiting for the new entrepreneur, well, to me, that's often a chain store.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's often somebody who's not from that neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And what we're looking for are the diversity of a commercial strip.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Manhattan is challenging.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I mean, I fight all the time for these mom and pops, and I'm often up against the big commercials.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Or vacancy after vacancy after vacancy.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Broadway is vacant.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And so, you know, look down here at Chambers Street.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: It's vacant.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: So I'm just saying, if you have some other ideas, let me know.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: But we need some teeth for the mom and pops.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: This panel is now excused.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lacey Tober, representing Brooklyn BP Antonio Reynoso, supports Intro 578's reforms to the IBZ Boundary Commission but warns convening the commission is risky given development pressures. She urges codifying IBZ protections through zoning changes and supporting industrial business solutions providers.
chapters.title: Lacey Tober testifies on Intro 578 for Brooklyn Borough President Reynoso

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I will now call the next panel, Lacey Tober, Nora Lewis, and Leah Archibald.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Lacey, you like to be, can begin?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Sure, I can start.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Thank you for holding this hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: I'm here representing Brooklyn Borough President Antonio Reynoso to provide testimony specifically on Intro 578.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Which would reform the city's industrial business zone boundary commission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: While the borough president feels that convening the commission is too risky at this time, for reasons I will explain, he does support the changes proposed in Intro 578.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: The bill will help protect industrial businesses by adding commission members to be appointed by the speaker and the public advocate and requiring more considerations to inform any proposed boundary change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Some background.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Mayor Bloomberg designated the 21 IBZs across the city in 2006 with the goal of supporting and preserving industrial businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: This designation included associated tax incentives and a commitment not to rezone land within the IBZs from manufacturing to residential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: However, recent administration...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: proposals such as DCP's NYC Industrial Plan and SPS's Business Solutions Center's RFP have left industrial businesses and the nonprofits that support them fighting to keep their land and their funding.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: In negotiations over the industrial plan, DCP referred to the IBZs as tax zones only and in their original draft proposed rezoning swaths of the IBZs for mixed use including residential.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Meanwhile, SBS is threatening to defund the critical industrial business solutions providers, IBSPs, who work with businesses and all the IBZs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: These policies are short-sighted because the industrial sector plays a critical role in the mayor's economic justice goals.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Manufacturing generally provides living wages with low barriers to entry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: I have a whole bunch of stats here about that for you that I don't have time to go through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: But rezoning changes across the city have led to a 5% decrease in land zone for manufacturing since 2010.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: And so that has led to a high demand for manufacturing space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Our goal then should be to strengthen the IBZs and secure protections for industrial jobs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: We don't need the IBZ Boundary Commission to do this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: We can and should achieve it through zoning change.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: DCP created new manufacturing zones in City of Yes for economic opportunity, and BP Reynoso is calling on this administration to codify IBZ protections promised in 2006

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: by mapping these zones within all the existing IBZ boundaries, and also critically to support the work of the IBZs across the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ki-Sung
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: This.

chapters.summary: Leah Archibald of Evergreen, a North Brooklyn local development corporation, supports Intro 578 and shares data showing industrial employment increased 9% in the North Brooklyn IBZ while 25% of industrial land was lost citywide. She warns developers are already approaching IBZ areas for residential conversion.
chapters.title: Leah Archibald of Evergreen testifies in support of Intro 578 and IBZ preservation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Hi, my name is Leah Archibald.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: I'm the executive director of Evergreen, and we're the local development corporation that works in industrial North Brooklyn to help small businesses, mostly manufacturers, grow so we can keep high-quality working-class jobs in our community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: We've been doing this work for over 40 years, and for 40 years we have learned a big lesson, and that is if we lose industrial land, we are not going to get it back, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: So we are here in support of Intro 578.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Some lessons learned from the rezoning of North Brooklyn in 2005.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Between 2002 and 2019, we've lost about 15% of our industrial jobs and lost 16 million square feet of M-zone land.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: That's about 25% of our industrial land that we lost in the rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: But another lesson we've learned is preservation works, right?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: At the same time, during those same years, in the North Brooklyn industrial business zone, right, which was protected, we've increased industrial employment by almost 9%.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: So this is really...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: This demonstrates that the industrial business zones, these are just not like random lines that are being drawn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: We believe that the past three administrations'promise not to rezone industrial business zone areas for residential uses has been the single most important factor

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: in the stabilization of New York City's industrial real estate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: You know, I think the time to address this, the Boundary Commission, really is now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: It's particularly in light of the Department of City Planning's Industrial Action Plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Okay, I guess I will finish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: You can go ahead and finish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: We think this will do a good job.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: You know, by broadening the commission, by giving it, by broadening the voice and creating a higher bar,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: by having a two-thirds vote to remove space from the industrial business zones, we think that this is going to lend additional protections and, you know, continue the industrial employment legacy in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Amauris Gurujung
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Nora Lewis of the Long Island City Partnership urges support for reforming the IBZ Boundary Commission, noting IBZs support 500,000 well-paid jobs. She describes opportunities to co-locate housing with light manufacturing in parts of the LIC IBZ and emphasizes the need for local voices in boundary decisions.
chapters.title: Nora Lewis of LIC Partnership testifies in support of Intro 578

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: Great.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: And yeah, just to echo agreement with everything that Lacey and Leah have just shared.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Thomas Henry and members of the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: My name is Nora Lewis, and I'm the business assistance manager at the Long Island City Partnership, the local nonprofit economic development organization serving Long Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: As the industrial business service provider for Western Queens, we manage both the LIC Business Improvement District and Industrial Business Zone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: I'm here to urge the Council to support the reform of the Industrial Business Zone Boundary Commission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: IBZs are crucial to preserving the city's industrial sector and the 500,000 well-paid jobs it supports, particularly for New Yorkers who are immigrants, people of color, and do not have a college degree.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: The industrial and manufacturing work done in IBZs is also critical to sustaining key supply chains and a wide network of small businesses across the five boroughs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: As the city's 21 IBZs contend with development pressures, there is a need to ensure the industrial sector continues to have the space, steady workforce, and legislative support to flourish.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: At the same time, there are portions of the LIC IBZ where there is an opportunity to co-locate housing with light manufacturing uses without displacement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: This new IBZ model could create a more connected neighborhood in LIC, particularly surrounding Queensbridge houses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: As every IBZ has nuances and different needs, it's important to have local voices involved in this important decision-making.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: Expanding membership of the IBZ Boundary Commission, emphasizing transparency, and reaffirming the comprehensive criteria Commission members must consider are paramount to this preservation and strengthening of the industrial sector, while also contending with

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: ambitious housing goals laid out by the city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: We urge the council to support this legislation to ensure New York City remains industrial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: New York City retains industrial businesses and fosters future growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Nora Lewis
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks for clarity on the panel's position about convening the commission. Tober, Archibald, and Lewis explain they support the legislation's reforms but believe convening is risky right now, with Archibald warning developers are already inquiring about residential conversion in IBZ areas.
chapters.title: Chair Thomas-Henry and panelists discuss nuances of convening the IBZ Boundary Commission

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I have a question or just a point of clarity.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Lacey, you mentioned convening the commission may be too risky, but then it sounds like you guys are in favor of the commission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: Of the revisions proposed in this legislation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: I think there's a nuance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: It's like convening the commission is not really something that we need to do right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: And I think we're worried that if we were to do that, given the makeup of the commission, even with these changes, there might be a push to shrink the zones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: And that's the opposite of what we want to do.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: However, in the case that the commission were to be convened, this legislation will help.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: With making sure that they're looking at a robust set of criteria for any changes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: It adds appointees from outside of the administration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: That might end up being a check on that effort, depending on the admin's priorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lacey Tober
utterances.text: So it's yes, but.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Anyone else want to give input into the pros and cons of the legislation?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: I think it's...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Not time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: There isn't a reason right now, I think, to convene the Boundary Revision Commission.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: But I really like the ideas to broaden the representation and raise the bar to pulling pieces out of the industrial business zones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: And I will also just like share this bit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: of neighborhood intel, you know, since the Department of City Planning released their industrial action plan and,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: you know, kind of raised the question about the future of industrial business zones, they sent a message to the real estate market.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: My office is getting visits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: From developers asking us how we would feel about residential in just a little corner of the industrial business zone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: And so I think we're going to be seeing private applications come through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Asking for residential conversion in the industrial business zones, and it's going to beg the question, like, what now?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: What is our commitment moving forward as a city?

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: So I think this legislation takes a step to try and prepare us for that, but I can tell you the developers are...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: On their way in.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And just to add to that, to shout out both Councilmember Gutierrez and all of the IBSPs who really did a lot of advocacy from the draft to the final version of that plan to convey that

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: they wanted to see changes and to see their districts protected and were able to be successful with that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Got it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: This panel is excused.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Leah Archibald
utterances.text: We will.

chapters.summary: Jessica Walker supports most of Intro 90's transparency provisions but opposes the mandatory lease extension, arguing it would hurt first-time and immigrant-owned businesses. She strongly supports Intro 874's voluntary incentive model and Intro 408's content creator pilot, and notes the chamber's free help desk at bizhelp.nyc.
chapters.title: Jessica Walker of Manhattan Chamber of Commerce testifies on Intro 90, 874, and 408

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chair and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: I'm Jessica Walker, president and CEO of the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We represent the borough's 125,000 businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: I'll start with Intro 90.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We support most of it, requiring a written lease, giving tenants clear disclosures about the space they're signing for, and posting model leases in multiple languages.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: These are simple, overdue protections, and we urge you to pass them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: But we cannot support the mandatory one-year extension at a capped rent.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: It's too small to save a struggling business and just large enough to change how every landlord in the city underwrites a lease.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: When it's harder to end the tenancy, owners get pickier about starting one.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Bigger deposits, personal guarantees, a preference for tenants with a strong balance sheet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The first time in immigrant-owned businesses we work with every day are the ones who can't clear that bar.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: A holdover doesn't fix the problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: It delays the same conversation by 12 months.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: The real problem.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: is that tenants arrive at renewal with no credible way to leave.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Relocating in Manhattan today means a year of dark rent, a permit gauntlet, and lost customers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: So the threat to walk away means nothing, and landlords are often negotiating from a place of strength.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Our research shows storefronts stay empty for years, not months, for the same reasons.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We will be releasing a full brief about this soon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: But long story short, if you make it possible to open a store in 90 days instead of a year, every tenant in the borough walks into a renewal with real alternatives if needed, and therefore a more balanced negotiation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: That's why we strongly support Intro 874.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: A preservation fund that pays property owners to offer 10-year leases puts money on the table.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: It's not a mandate.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: It's the deal both sides will sign.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We also support Intro 408.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Small businesses tell us marketing is where they feel most outgunned.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: A content creator pilot is low cost and worth running.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: We tested something similar and know it can work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Finally, to any business owner listening, if you're facing a lease question, a permit, a fine, I was just going to say go to bizhelp.nyc.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: That's our free help desk, and we'll get you an answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jessica Walker
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Next up is Catherine.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: You may begin.

chapters.summary: Catherine Mursak, a worker-owner at a Chelsea yoga cooperative, testifies that long leases don't help if businesses can't afford rising rent. She urges the Council to advance commercial rent stabilization legislation, distinguishing it from rent control, and disputes claims that commercial rents remain below pre-pandemic levels.
chapters.title: Catherine Mursak of Samamkaya Yoga urges commercial rent stabilization

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify online today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: I really appreciate the council's efforts and the bills being discussed today, but New York needs commercial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: commercial rent stabilization so that small businesses can survive, not just open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: My name is Catherine Mursak, and I'm a worker owner at Samamkaya Yoga Back Care and Scoliosis Collective, a worker-owned cooperative yoga studio providing therapeutic classes online and in Chelsea.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: In my cooperative business, we invested in a studio space for people with differently shaped bodies and abilities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: As a democratic workplace, our teachers all have a vote in important decisions about the business.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: We negotiated a 10-year lease on our space, which we have specially built out for our needs with the yoga rope walls and storage shelves and took out a lot of loans to do that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: But rising rent still leaves our future uncertain.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Our small studio space has limits to how many students we can host and how much we can ask our students to pay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: A long lease is not security if we cannot afford to stay.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: The Storefront Business Bill of Rights offers really useful protections, but temporary extensions cannot replace lasting affordability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Grants for legacy businesses should secure affordable rent, not merely a lease term.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: And a private right of action is only useful to business owners who can actually afford that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Every year, countless well-loved and viable businesses are forced to close or move out of their community because landlords jack up their rent as soon as they see that the business is doing well or that the neighborhood is gentrifying.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: And I disagree with the alleged claim that commercial rents overall remain below pre-pandemic levels, and I would really like to see the data that backs up that claim.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Please advance a city commercial rent stabilization bill to introduction, a hearing and passage, carrying forward Fair Rent NYC's recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Please note we're referring to this as commercial rent stabilization, not control, to promote reasonable rent increases and prevent the kind of doubling and tripling of rent that was raised by Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: We're not asking for commercial rent freezes, as the name commercial rent control would suggest.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Time expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Okay, I just wanted to say that there's another Catherine Mursik, and that's my colleague, Olympia Kazi.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: She didn't receive a link.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: So if you could call her as well, I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: And I will submit a written testimony for the rest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Catherine Mursak
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.text: Community-based organizations often have more detailed data on their local neighborhood businesses than is available citywide.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell
utterances.text: valuable resources to legislators and SBS on intro 874.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Sewell

utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Lisa Sorin of the Bronx Chamber of Commerce supports Intro 408, noting that AI training and website creation programs have been among the chamber's most popular offerings. She argues the bill bridges the digital divide and positions NYC as a national leader in leveraging the creative economy for local development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Thank you to the council for your continued engagement and collaboration with the small business community on issues that impact affordability, stability, and economic growth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: I am submitting testimony in support of 0408, which would establish a pilot program to match small businesses with social media content creators for assistance in marketing and advertising.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: I first want to extend my thanks to Councilmember Riley, who has shown continued leadership and dedication to supporting New York City's entrepreneurs and helping small businesses thrive.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Although many entrepreneurs are eager to engage more effectively on social media, oftentimes they lack the resources, expertise, or time to do so.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Through the Small Business Resource Network, the Chamber has seen this firsthand.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: For example, programs such as an AI training in partnership with Google and

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Website creation services have been among the most popular programs, demonstrating a growing eagerness to engage and advertise digitally.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Council member Riley's legislation represents a crucial step in bridging the digital divide for our small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: It has the potential to deliver real measurable impact by increasing foot traffic for storefronts, boosting neighborhoods, supporting job creation, and fostering media literacy and marketing ability among the small business community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: It also positions New York City as a national leader in policies that leverage a creative economy to advance local economic development.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Overall, we encourage the council to advance and adopt 408.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: We also stand ready to work with the council and SBS in ensuring this program reaches as many small businesses as possible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Lisa Sorin
utterances.text: Thank you for your opportunity to testify and for your ongoing commitment to supporting New York City's entrepreneurs and small businesses.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

summary: The Committee on Small Business held a hearing on four bills: Intro 90 (Storefront Business Bill of Rights), Intro 408 (social media content creator matching pilot), Intro 578 (IBZ Boundary Commission reform), and Intro 874 (Legacy Business Registry and Preservation Fund).

SBS Chief of Staff Haris Khan testified on the agency's recent initiatives and expressed support for the goals of all four bills while noting concerns about operational details, particularly around the legacy business fund and the social media matching program.

Public testimony included strong support from BIDs, chambers of commerce, and small business advocates, with several witnesses urging the Council to also pursue commercial rent stabilization, while real estate brokers and REBNY raised concerns about Intro 90's mandatory lease extension provision.
